issues.description:
## Outcome

Prove exactly one preselected business task end to end: receive the user's data and problem, form/present the task and missing-data guidance in step2, obtain step3 sign-off (otherwise repeat step2), then have Codex use OpenAI Data for the bounded analysis/modeling needed by that task, verify results and deliver its one final business output. Select and lock the task/input/output contract once in <issue id="6725bd06-92b0-4374-ad59-9d23c30448c5" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-24">DSC-24</issue>. Retail replenishment is the selected single task; its deliverable is one final report containing the item-and-quantity restocking list and concise relevant EDA/feature findings and limitations. No customer app/executable, generic task router or additional use case is required.

The prepared retail dataset is this MVP's engineering fixture. User intake still begins with their files and problem; absent data is reported in step2. Execution uses the same versioned task approved by the user, with no separate post-sign-off task-definition stage.

## Completion gate

- [ ] Step6 initial-model/baseline evidence precedes step7 LLM-generated additional features; step8 compares model/feature options before frozen unseen validation. Feature outputs and leakage checks are verified, and relevant findings appear in the final report.
- [ ] Routine analysis progress remains internal; relevant step5 findings are included in the final customer report. Material clarifications/blockers still receive targeted handling.
- [ ] All implementation sub-issues are complete and their acceptance criteria verified.
- [ ] Runtime evidence, tests and versioned artifacts are linked; a diagram alone is not implementation completion.
- [ ] Recorded demo, actual Codex/Data execution evidence and the delivered business output are reviewable.
- [ ] Reviewer accepts the milestone outcome before the next milestone starts.

## Sequence

First milestone: build the MVP before individual workflow expansion.
This gate blocks the next milestone's implementation issues.

## Review status

Proposed implementation plan in Backlog. Dates, estimates and new assignments are intentionally unset for discussion.

## Architecture

Reuse working MVP components in V1. LangChain handles understanding, structured task packets and humanized output; LangGraph is used where state, branching or confirmation/resume is needed. DeepAgents later composes the ten workflows within the same V1. Codex uses OpenAI's Data plugin (`data-analytics`, displayed as Data) for analytical authoring and execution in its supported environment. The parent approves the task/run contract, verifies returned evidence and controls transitions. Verify the supported plugin-enabled invocation through <issue id="776aee5b-44ab-43cb-b34b-7e217bd4b618" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-26">DSC-26</issue>; do not assume an external `@Data` API or substitute Code Interpreter without an explicit scope decision. Deliver the requested business output; a restocking request ends with an item-and-quantity list. Customer app/executable delivery is outside this scope.

[Source Miro section](<https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVEajrXz8=/?moveToWidget=3458764686970454504>)

## Parent verification — required before Done

This parent issue verifies **milestone implementation completeness**, in addition to the runtime parent's separate per-run checks. [Single-case verification and evidence](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-56>) defines the scoped MVP checklist. A fixed evidence ledger and named reviewer suffice; no reusable V1 verification engine is required.

### Requirements and evidence ledger

For each child issue below, expand **every acceptance criterion** into a ledger row: source requirement → implementation/artifact → repeatable verification/check → expected result → actual result → evidence/version → verifier → Pass / Fail / Blocked. A checked box or implementer's claim without evidence is not proof.

* [DSC-24 — M01.01 — Lock retail restocking dataset and output contract](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-24>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-25 — M01.02 — Build retail capability assessment and initial customer sign-off](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-25>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-26 — M01.03 — Integrate Codex with OpenAI Data and verify real analytical execution](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-26>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-27 — M01.04 — Execute cleanup, EDA and initial features](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-27>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-28 — M01.05 — Implement initial benchmark, LLM feature generation, comparison and validation](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-28>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-29 — M01.06 — Prepare the requested final business output](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-29>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-30 — M01.07 — Verify and deliver the final business output](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-30>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-31 — M01.08 — Record the real demonstration and collect review evidence](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-31>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-10 — M01 — Implement MVP human interaction and guardrail contract](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-10>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.
* [DSC-56 — M01.09 — Verify the single retail restocking demo and evidence](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-56>): verify every acceptance criterion, not only the title or happy path.

### Milestone-specific verification checklist

- [ ] Exactly one named task, prepared dataset and final-output contract are locked; the demo completes that task only. A second task or generalized task support is not an acceptance requirement.
- [ ] Real input loading and initial understanding/sign-off are demonstrated for the selected case; any material corrections preserve the same task boundary.
- [ ] <issue id="776aee5b-44ab-43cb-b34b-7e217bd4b618" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-26">DSC-26</issue> proves a supported Codex invocation with OpenAI Data enabled and actual analytical execution; unresolved integration cannot be treated as passed.
- [ ] Measured baseline/comparison artifacts are genuine; development windows end by the cutoff, winner and final acceptance rule are frozen before holdout, and failed final validation blocks delivery without holdout-driven tuning.
- [ ] The delivered output matches the confirmed business task, fields, units and rules; a restocking request yields one final report with the item-and-quantity list and concise verified EDA/feature findings.
- [ ] Output values, logs, versions and limitations agree. No customer app/executable or mandatory separate report is required.

### Verification and rework loop

1. Confirm the previous gate is accepted and inspect all source requirements, child criteria, handoff contracts and explicit scope decisions.
2. Check implementation and versioned evidence; run repeatable relevant checks in the approved environment. Cover normal behavior, edge cases, expected failure branches and affected regressions; review user-facing usability.
3. If evidence is absent/stale, a requirement is unmapped, a child is incomplete or a check fails: keep this parent open, record the discrepancy, and return/reopen the affected child issue with a concrete correction request. The next milestone remains blocked.
4. Apply only authorized corrections. Rerun failed and affected regression checks against the new code/artifact versions; invalidate any dependent stale approval. Repeat within explicit retry/time/compute budgets. Unresolved uncertainty or exhausted budgets goes to review, never automatic approval.
5. Name the verifier and record the final ledger/report, exact artifacts, commands/environment and a Pass / Fail / Blocked decision. Close this gate only when every required criterion passes and the milestone outcome is accepted.

### Closure rules

- [ ] Every child issue is complete with current evidence; no requirement or defect is silently waived.
- [ ] Complete evidence ledger, milestone-specific checks and passing regression results are linked.
- [ ] Output/handoff contracts match the next milestone's input contract; customer-output usability, correctness and requested format are reviewed where applicable.
- [ ] A named verifier explicitly accepts the outcome and records remaining limitations. Material scope changes require recorded approval and updated requirements.
- [ ] Completion-gate decision and current passing report agree before downstream execution advances.

Native Linear dependencies organize implementation order. The MVP parent must enforce this run's checkpoint decisions; a named reviewer verifies current artifacts and the fixed acceptance ledger before closing this milestone. Do not add a shared reusable runner or a cross-V1 enforcement platform to M01.

Successful testing of an expected model-run failure branch can satisfy implementation acceptance. It does **not** approve advancing that failed model run. Verification must never optimize or reselect a frozen model using final holdout outcomes.

## Step9 failure branch — customer run outcome

A failed frozen validation goes to an internal parent evidence check. If failure is confirmed, a bounded correction still fails, or the cause cannot be resolved within MVP limits, deliver a concise verified explanation that this MVP could not produce a reliable solution for the requested task using the supplied data/scope. Record the actual reason and distinguish execution failure from genuine model underperformance. End that run without a restocking recommendation, second-best-model fallback, holdout tuning or indefinite review.

This is an expected terminal customer response, not a claim that the business problem is universally impossible. Correctly handling it can satisfy failure-branch checks; it does not mark a failed model run successful or alone satisfy the existing successful end-to-end restocking demonstration requirement.

## Selected retail scope and data readiness

The one required case uses the supplied2022–2025 sales CSV/dictionary plus matching, separately stored synthetic inventory and ordering-rule datasets. The 2016 workbook and former nine input-scenario bundles are superseded for active MVP requirements. Do not require building or demonstrating those extra cases.

The final output is one illustrative restocking list. Missing-input capability guidance remains a guardrail if needed within this task; it does not replace actual full-input execution. Cleanup/target/missingness/model choices remain agent-owned, with only irreducible consequential business facts escalated.

All ten child issues contain future implementation prompts and shared data links. Gate closure still requires real Codex/OpenAI Data invocation, measured benchmark/candidate evidence, frozen untouched holdout, verified stock/receipt/rounding arithmetic and actual delivered list. Fixture checks alone do not complete this gate. Miro remains read-only; no V1 expansion or app delivery.

## Shared data — one retail restocking case

Canonical shared home: [Retail MVP — Restocking list](<https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XgeA1GBRUsB4azuDdR1w-PxJ0CPMH85d>), inside the user's [Datasets folder](<https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1F0168Oal9k6LO05xyXicgo31ETmhAsqP>). Files are uploaded and their Drive parent/size metadata has been read back.

Three separate datasets for this SAME task:

* **Synthetic ordering rules:** [ordering_policy.csv](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1QT3Xk6ecm7AJDS9z0MJGaU_2U5dTga5v/view?usp=drivesdk>) has 336 policies, with supplier lead times, seven-day review, explicit safety stock, minimums and order multiples.

Source completeness remains unverified; sparse product/store dates cannot automatically become zero. Investigate exact duplicates, eight nonpositive quantity records, returns/cancellations and status casing autonomously.

[Explanation](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NUcILz5_YBmBe-S0ZAPpW5R5-AG6plNX/view?usp=drivesdk>), [generation manifest](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/18caKbFe7PuwM_mrAkR75jR5PBg0u3EnR/view?usp=drivesdk>), [generator](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Syo-FqmcWKtwBEakxpblk1J0QkN4PIfc/view?usp=drivesdk>), [source QA](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sLd2Zdd2SmE5XX8U1LgMU8dUU1GLqldD/view?usp=drivesdk>) and [reproducible QA notebook](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1iDvqKHgJW61IaL-O4Yh4C7u3_Ya86H7V/view?usp=drivesdk>) are in Drive Documentation. issues.description:
## Goal

Create the shared architecture for SuiroAI and its relationship to DSCraft.

## Current product scope — updated 2026-10-16

DSCraft is the free/open-source data-science pipeline library; SuiroAI is the closed-source agentic platform built around/with it.

MVP supports exactly one task selected once through <issue id="6725bd06-92b0-4374-ad59-9d23c30448c5" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-24">DSC-24</issue>. Fixed flow: (1) user supplies data and states the problem → (2) parent forms the proposed task, identifies missing data and feeds the proposal back → (3) user signs off, or correction/rejection returns to step2 → execute that same approved task using Codex/OpenAI Data → parent verifies evidence → requested final business output. Missing data is explained in step2 and new inputs repeat that step. There is no separate task-definition step after sign-off.

For the restocking request, deliver one final report containing the item-and-quantity restocking list and concise relevant EDA/feature findings and limitations. Routine analytical progress remains internal until that final report. Customer app/executable delivery, hosting and a separate technical-report artifact are outside scope. Retail restocking is the selected M01 task; <issue id="6725bd06-92b0-4374-ad59-9d23c30448c5" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-24">DSC-24</issue> locks its active data/output contract. No further business-task selection is required.

Internal cleanup, analysis, modeling and verification serve that one result. No generic task selection/routing or additional use case is required for M01; broader support belongs to later V1.

## Component boundaries

* User/UI: supply files and request, confirm understanding, receive the requested output.
* LangChain: focused prompt/understanding and humanizer calls with typed task/output contracts; roles do not require separate autonomous agents.
* Parent/orchestration: control stage transitions, approved task/run contracts, evidence checks, failure/review paths and final delivery. Use LangGraph where explicit state, branching or confirmation/resume is needed.
* Analytical worker: Codex uses OpenAI's Data plugin (`data-analytics`, displayed as Data). Use its supported execution environment; building a separate custom runtime is not an MVP requirement.
* Integration boundary: <issue id="776aee5b-44ab-43cb-b34b-7e217bd4b618" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-26">DSC-26</issue> must prove supported plugin-enabled Codex invocation, file/task transfer and result/evidence retrieval. Do not assume an external `@Data` API. Code Interpreter is a distinct option, not a silent replacement.
* Human interaction/guardrails: explicit initial sign-off, autonomous context-aware cleanup, internal progress/evidence with findings in the final report, parent run approval, data isolation, budgets, audit evidence and stop/review paths.
* ML/DSCraft: initial preparation/features → step6 initial-model/baseline gate → step7 LLM-generated additional feature definitions implemented and checked by Codex/Data → step8 bounded model/feature comparison → frozen winner and untouched final holdout. Retain training-only preprocessing and reuse appropriate DSCraft capabilities. This is one approved analytical task, not separate autonomous phase agents.
* Delivery/observability: customer receives the agreed output; retain versioned code, data/split/model references, execution logs and checks internally.

## Product sequence

M01 proves the simplified input-to-output MVP. M02–M11 expand its reusable components into ten individual workflows. M12 composes those workflows under DeepAgents within the same V1, retaining Codex with Data as the analytical worker.

## Done when

- [ ] Major components and typed interfaces are shown.
- [ ] DSCraft vs SuiroAI boundary is explicit.
- [ ] MVP vs later V1 components are distinguishable.
- [ ] Supported Codex/Data integration is evidenced or clearly marked unresolved.
- [ ] Final delivery is the requested business output; model validation and verification remain explicit.
- [ ] Team has reviewed the architecture and implementation work is captured in Linear.

[Full architecture and workflow map](<https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVEajrXz8=/>)

The 2026-10-16 user-directed scope above supersedes older executable-delivery/separate-custom-runtime wording in the visual map until that map is reconciled. Linear remains a Backlog implementation plan; this edit does not mark engineering complete.

## Selected task and Miro boundary

M01 targets exactly one retail replenishment case, using the supplied Sales_transactions_2022_2025.csv and sales dictionary plus separately stored synthetic inventory/receipt and ordering-rule datasets. Shared data is in [Retail MVP — Restocking list](<https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XgeA1GBRUsB4azuDdR1w-PxJ0CPMH85d>); [DSC-24](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-24>) and the [single-case contract](<https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/document/retail-mvp-single-restocking-case-shared-data-and-implementation-72e8278521db>) hold the active input/output contract. Use Product_ID/Store_ID, historical review2025-11-30 and product units. The old2016 workbook/supplements and additional scenario bundles are outside the active demo. One customer deliverable: a final report containing an illustrative restocking list and concise verified EDA/feature findings. Miro is read-only; no diagram changes or product implementation are claimed.

contract.content:
# Retail MVP — one restocking case

## Scope and current status

Solve one retail replenishment task end to end and deliver one final report containing the restocking list plus concise relevant EDA/feature findings and material limitations. Data preparation, demand modeling, benchmark comparison and verification support that output; they are not separate customer deliverables. No application, dashboard, extra business case or general verification platform is required.

Current work is documentation, future implementation prompts, source-data QA and generated synthetic operational inputs. No SuiroAI pipeline, model or restocking recommendation has been implemented. All MVP issues stay in Backlog until implementation and actual evidence exist. Miro is a read-only architecture reference.

## Shared data — one retail restocking case

Canonical shared home: [Retail MVP — Restocking list](<https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XgeA1GBRUsB4azuDdR1w-PxJ0CPMH85d>), inside the user's [Datasets folder](<https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1F0168Oal9k6LO05xyXicgo31ETmhAsqP>). Files are uploaded and their Drive parent/size metadata has been read back.

Three separate datasets for this SAME task:

* **Sales history:** [Sales_transactions_2022_2025.csv](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1y_CcJa6-esM-zc8GZNoO5g_beXwjGHQ2/view?usp=drivesdk>) and [supplied sales dictionary](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Oen4dciFAOAjVyJYR6FRrZl8wP-foNkV/view?usp=drivesdk>). 18,045 raw rows, 45 exact duplicates, 18,000 distinct records; 28 products, 12 stores, 336 Product_ID/Store_ID pairs, 2022-01-01–2025-12-31.
* **Synthetic inventory:** [inventory_position.csv](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AI5T9KMNLmHWQH0YBp9WPda_2PPrTKVd/view?usp=drivesdk>) has 336 usable-stock snapshots; [inbound_deliveries.csv](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1h1GfN1PRgbZ7eGVCtTLKwXcOiJBIVCqU/view?usp=drivesdk>) has 126 due-dated incoming-order lines. The ledger explicitly has no open orders for the other 210 keys. On_Order_Qty summarizes these receipt lines; never count both.
* **Synthetic ordering rules:** [ordering_policy.csv](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1QT3Xk6ecm7AJDS9z0MJGaU_2U5dTga5v/view?usp=drivesdk>) has 336 policies, with supplier lead times, seven-day review, explicit safety stock, minimums and order multiples.

Historical review date: **2025-11-30**. Use the same-SKU **product_unit**, supported by the dictionary's Quantity definition. All operational rows are marked synthetic. Seed 20261016; only records/keys available through the cutoff size these generated facts. Proposed final untouched holdout: December 2025. The raw source retains future records; implementation must enforce temporal boundaries.

Inventory_Level is approximate stock at transaction, not a verified as-of usable-stock snapshot. Delivery_Days is customer fulfillment duration, not supplier replenishment lead time. Source completeness remains unverified; sparse product/store dates cannot automatically become zero. Investigate exact duplicates, eight nonpositive quantity records, returns/cancellations and status casing autonomously.

[Explanation](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NUcILz5_YBmBe-S0ZAPpW5R5-AG6plNX/view?usp=drivesdk>), [generation manifest](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/18caKbFe7PuwM_mrAkR75jR5PBg0u3EnR/view?usp=drivesdk>), [generator](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Syo-FqmcWKtwBEakxpblk1J0QkN4PIfc/view?usp=drivesdk>), [source QA](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sLd2Zdd2SmE5XX8U1LgMU8dUU1GLqldD/view?usp=drivesdk>) and [reproducible QA notebook](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1iDvqKHgJW61IaL-O4Yh4C7u3_Ya86H7V/view?usp=drivesdk>) are in Drive Documentation. Local working copy: `data/retail_mvp/sales_2022_2025/`.

This replaces the 2016 Numbers workbook and its Product_Code/Warehouse supplements for the active MVP. Do not mix them. The extra R01–R09 dataset bundles are not required for this MVP. Retain truthful missing-input behavior as a guardrail, not a second deliverable or nine-case execution project. No model, pipeline, restocking output or app has been implemented; the supplied source files remain unchanged.

## What the generated datasets contain

**Inventory is one coherent dataset with two tables.** Inventory_Position records usable stock per Product_ID/Store_ID at the review date and an open-order summary. Inbound_Deliveries records incoming quantities, order dates and expected arrival dates. The summary reconciles to the complete synthetic ledger. Missing real receipts would not imply zero; the synthetic zero-open-order rule is explicit for this dataset.

**Ordering rules are their own dataset.** Each product/store pair has assumed supplier lead time 1–7 calendar days, review period seven days, order multiple 1/5/10 product units, a minimum positive order of one multiple and an explicit safety-stock quantity. These are test assumptions, not supplier contracts recovered from sales history.

Operational stock and buffers use seeded variation scaled by typical positive transaction quantity from exact-deduplicated pre-cutoff rows. This is arbitrary input sizing, not a forecast or a daily demand estimate. No missing sales dates are zero-filled by the generator. Source Inventory_Level and Delivery_Days are preserved for inspection but not promoted to operational stock or supplier policy.

The supplied sales dictionary covers all 36 columns and resolves transaction identifiers and quantity units. Origin/license, extract completeness, missing product/store-date meanings and operational availability are not established merely by receiving the file. Cost/currency/budget optimization is outside this single task.

## MVP intake loop and preparation boundary

1. **User supplies data and states the problem.** Capture their original request and files as supplied. The prepared demonstration data is an engineering fixture, not a requirement to submit already joined/cleaned tables and not a substitute silently loaded when the user provides no data.
2. **Parent forms and presents the proposed task.** Read the request and inspect the actual supplied material read-only; propose the understood goal, output, input references, context, material assumptions and gaps. Tell the user what data is missing and why when files were absent, inaccessible or insufficient. Candidate relationships may be identified, but no joins/cleanup/modeling run here. Feed the proposed task back in plain language.
3. **User signs off or returns to step2.** Approval binds to the current proposal/input version and permits execution of that same task. Rejection, corrections or new material data repeat step2; no response waits. Receiving requested missing data also repeats step2 before sign-off.

There is no separate post-sign-off task-definition step. Parent code/run approval and execution configuration are internal execution controls. Actual joining, cleaning and preparation occur in <issue id="40e6417e-d6eb-45da-980f-69c5eb2880de" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-27">DSC-27</issue> after the supported task is approved. Ordinary statistical decisions remain agent-owned; ask only for irreducible material business facts.

## Future implementation prompt

Inspect the supplied files and dictionary, confirm the customer's requested list and material synthetic assumptions once, and pass one bounded task contract to Codex with OpenAI Data enabled through an actually verified supported invocation. Do not assume an external @Data API or silently substitute Code Interpreter.

Prepare Product_ID/Store_ID history from transaction records. Preserve raw data and hashes; reconcile exact duplicates instead of dropping shared Order_ID lines. Normalize status casing; justify returns, cancellations, processing/shipped orders and nonpositive quantities. Define the modeled sales target explicitly. Investigate sparse series and whether absent dates can defensibly represent zero; use pooled/sparse-demand methods or supported fallbacks when suitable. Do not equate recorded sales with unobserved true demand.

The agent owns aggregation, missingness treatment, feature selection, baseline/model choice and routine statistical decisions. Use only prediction-time-available features; do not silently use realized customer delivery duration, end-state returns/status or approximate inventory as a demand predictor. Ask for only an irreducible material business fact after investigation/sensitivity, never customer choice of imputation or hyperparameters.

Proposed chronology: develop from 2022–2024; rolling development validation January–November2025 with every target window ending by November30; freeze population, transforms, target rules, candidate selection, metrics and the final pass/fail acceptance rule before untouched December2025 evaluation. Score fully observed holdout horizons only; a failed final gate blocks delivery without tuning, and December outcomes cannot affect the November30 list. Use equal origins, horizons and eligible populations for the baseline and bounded candidate shortlist. A better measured result follows the proceed branch; worse pauses with evidence; equal enters review. Report uncertainty honestly, without holdout-driven tuning or operational-benefit claims.

Forecast over supplier lead time plus seven-day review, add the declared safety stock, subtract usable stock and only inbound quantities that arrive in time, clamp net need at zero, then apply minimums/multiples when an order is positive. Verify timing within the protection period: a late receipt cannot cure an earlier shortage. Never subtract both the on-order summary and receipt ledger. Trace all quantities to source/scenario inputs.

Deliver one list with Product_ID, Product_Name when reliably mapped, Store_ID, OrderQty and Quantity_Unit. Include a needed-by date only when required. Clearly mark the list illustrative because stock and supplier rules are synthetic. Include a concise business-relevant EDA/feature summary and material limitations in that same final customer report. Keep routine progress, detailed forecasts, code, logs, metrics and verification evidence internal.

## Helpful missing-input behavior

If supplied inputs do not support the list, explain what they support, the specific missing material facts, and what those facts would unlock. For example: “With sales history I can estimate recorded sales. Add usable stock, incoming orders and supplier ordering rules to calculate net replenishment.”

Do not give a blanket “this tool is not for you” refusal, invent stock or supplier facts, or silently replace the list with a forecast or summary. A narrower output requires confirmation of a changed objective. Routine statistical work does not require repeated customer sign-offs.

Missing-input behavior remains an MVP guardrail. The prior R01–R09 matrix is deferred reference material, not a requirement to build or execute nine datasets before this one demonstration.

## Feature-generation and comparison sequence

Step6 evaluates the initial model against the baseline using the initial prepared features. After that checkpoint, step7 uses the LLM to generate additional feature definitions and transformation logic from task context, EDA and development-only model errors. Codex/Data builds and validates those features using past-only information and training-fold-fitted transformations. The parent checks definitions, outputs, timing and leakage controls.

Step8 then compares a bounded model shortlist and original/augmented feature options on the same eligible records, origins, horizons and metrics. Generated features must earn inclusion through measured development results. Freeze the winning feature pipeline and model before unseen validation. The final holdout is not visible to feature generation or selection. Keep useful feature explanations and measured contribution for the final report; no interim analysis-progress update.

This required LLM-driven feature-generation stage is distinct from optional learned neural-representation extraction, which remains outside the fixed MVP requirement.

## Step9 failure handling

When frozen unseen-data validation fails, pause recommendation delivery and have the parent review the evidence: input versions, source/split integrity, metric calculations, frozen model/feature configuration and code/runtime failures. This is an internal parent check, not an automatic customer sign-off.

Correct a demonstrable implementation or calculation defect only within the existing retry/compute limits and approved task. Log the defect, correction and affected recheck. Any re-execution must retain the predeclared model, feature definitions, acceptance rule and temporal boundaries; failure evidence cannot justify tuning, reselection, changing the threshold or trying the second-best model.

If the checks confirm genuine underperformance, the corrected frozen run still fails, or the issue cannot be resolved within the MVP's limits, end the run with a verified customer-facing explanation. State that this MVP could not produce a reliable solution for the requested task using the supplied data and allowed scope. Give the evidenced reason and material limitation; do not claim the problem is universally impossible.

For confirmed model underperformance, an appropriate message is: “We could not produce a reliable restocking recommendation from the supplied data within this MVP. The model failed the agreed validation requirement after we checked the result.” If validation could not be completed because of an unresolved execution/data defect, say that instead of inventing a measured model failure.

Return a terminal validation_failed or execution_failed outcome as appropriate. Do not calculate or deliver a purportedly valid restocking list, automatically try the runner-up, restart model search or remain in an indefinite review loop. Retain diagnostic evidence internally and provide the concise final failure explanation to the customer.

## Completion evidence

Require real supported Codex/Data execution; time-safe source preparation and benchmark/candidate evidence; frozen untouched holdout evaluation; reconciled stock/receipt/ordering arithmetic; and one verified delivered restocking list. Version source and synthetic input hashes, task/assumption packet, actual logs, measured metrics, final artifact and parent verification decisions.

Fixture-data validity or a correct incomplete-input explanation alone does not complete the MVP. No real stockout, profit or inventory-cost improvement can be proved from this sales extract and synthetic operational inputs.

## Architecture reference

The existing [MVP architecture outline](<https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVEajrXz8=/?moveToWidget=3458764686970454504>) supports intake understanding/confirmation, autonomous analytical work, parent checks and humanized output. LangChain supplies focused understanding/task/output calls; use LangGraph only where state, branching or resume is needed. One parent and one bounded staged Codex/Data task suffice for this MVP. Miro is not changed.

## Miro-to-MVP implementation alignment

Use the existing [Miro MVP frame](<https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVEajrXz8=/?moveToWidget=3458764686970454504>) as read-only workflow evidence. This review read its live81-item frame. The user's later scope instructions control where its older app/runtime wording differs.

| -- | -- |
| One prepared task and parent specification | <issue id="6725bd06-92b0-4374-ad59-9d23c30448c5" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-24">DSC-24</issue> locks the retail contract; <issue id="b0d7413d-13ed-4fc5-abb1-26e9f9c8e6c6" href="https://linear.app/gr3enarr0w/issue/DSC-10">DSC-10</issue> defines guardrails |

Parent checkpoints, internal progress/evidence, bounded correction/recheck, worse/equal baseline review and final-validation failure blocking are retained. Cleanup/EDA/feature findings are communicated in the final report, with no interim customer analysis-progress update. Routine analytical decisions remain agent-owned; irreducible material-fact clarifications and genuine blocker messages still occur when needed. Separate phase agents, neural feature extraction, reusable V1 verification infrastructure, mandatory report/charts, executable delivery and a separate custom runtime are not M01 requirements. No Miro items were changed.

Final-holdout acceptance (metric/direction, threshold/tolerance and minimum coverage) must be frozen before scoring; failure blocks delivery. Development target windows end by November 30, 2025; December scoring uses fully observed horizons only. December outcomes never affect the November30 list. These are future implementation requirements, not claims that tests or modeling have run.
